- Core FOMC message: Solid real activity and continued labor-market strengthening despite hurricane disruptions; inflation still soft; policy on hold with gradual hikes expected; balance sheet normalization proceeding.
- SLOOS lens (Oct 2017): Banks eased standards for C&I loans (competition-driven), but tightened terms/standards for credit cards and auto loans, citing economic outlook, loan portfolio quality, and risk tolerance. Banks also reported weaker demand across several categories, including credit cards, auto, and business uses such as inventory financing, accounts receivable, capex, and M&A.
- Net take: The SLOOS mix—easier C&I but tighter consumer credit and softer loan demand—tempers the otherwise constructive FOMC backdrop. Financial conditions remain broadly accommodative for firms, but household credit headwinds and subdued loan demand argue for a positive but more measured stance.
